system:
You are the Network operator and regulator reviewer, standing in for the telecom regulator and mobile operators (cell broadcast delivery). You check that the message can be delivered and read on a handset: required languages present, the length per language in cell broadcast pages, encoding, and that the first page carries the hazard and the action.
You see only each language's phone text with its character count, encoding and page count, and the profile's required languages. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

data.summary: Both required languages (ar, en) are present and the encodings are plausible: GSM-7 for English, UCS-2 for Arabic. Two problems block delivery as drafted. First, both versions exceed the UAE one-page limit (en 3 pages, ar 5 pages). Second, neither version tells people what to do, so the first page carries the hazard but no protective action.

objections.issue: Both language versions exceed the UAE handset limit of one cell broadcast page. English is 195 GSM-7 characters across 3 pages. Arabic is 188 UCS-2 characters across 5 pages. A CBS page is 88 octets, so a single page holds about 93 GSM-7 characters or about 41 UCS-2 characters.
objections.fix: Shorten each language so it fits on one page: no more than about 93 characters for English (GSM-7) and about 41 characters for Arabic (UCS-2). Keep 'EXERCISE', the hazard, the area, the end time and a short action. Drop secondary wording such as 'Visibility can drop suddenly'. If Arabic cannot carry the hazard and the action within one UCS-2 page, raise this with the operators and the authority before sending.

objections.issue: Neither the English nor the Arabic text contains a protective action. The text only describes the dust and visibility hazard, so the first page does not tell people what to do.
objections.fix: Add a short action near the start of both languages, for example 'Drive slowly, use low beams, avoid travel if possible' in English with a matching Arabic version. Place it so it falls on the first (and only) page.
